headline: Approved state funds for Putnam Terrace at 344-350 Putnam Avenue and a new IT administrator position in the 2026-2027 budget.
summary: Council backed a Connecticut Climate Superfund and approved the Mill River Trail design project. It voted 8-1-1 to continue Edward Page Reynolds as police chief and accepted a fleet replacement proposal, 8-2. The Administration removed a $26k crossing guard transfer and sidewalk contract extensions, and a $70,000 special education review was not discussed.
decisions: Approved Amendment #2 of the engineering and environmental consulting services agreement, 11 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 abstention.
Approved a master municipal agreement with the state for rights of way projects, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved the project authorization letter with the state for the Mill River Trail design project, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved accepting and spending state funds for brownfield remediation at Putnam Terrace, 344-350 Putnam Avenue, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved a resolution supporting the establishment of a Connecticut Climate Superfund, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved applying for and, if awarded, accepting and spending 2026 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant funds, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved the mayoral appointment of Jermaine B. Atkinson as assistant fire chief, 12 in favor, 0 opposed.
Approved continued employment of Edward Page Reynolds as police chief, 8 in favor, 1 opposed, 1 abstention.
Approved amending the 2026-2027 budget to create an information technology administrator position, 9 in favor, 1 opposed.
Approved submission calendar items 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4, including 14 CDBG subrecipient agreements, all in favor.
Accepted a fleet replacement proposal for the Town's highest-priority vehicles, 8 in favor, 2 opposed.
Removed from the agenda by the Administration: the 2026-2027 HPD budget amendment and $26k transfer for crossing guards.
Removed from the agenda by the Administration: extensions of three sidewalk replacement vendor agreements.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, 
CONNECTICUT 
 
LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL 
OCTOBER 5, 2026  
 
MINUTES DRAFT 
 
 
 
 
Present - Katie Kiely, President 
Present - Sean Cardwell, Pro Tem 
Present - Sarah Gallagher, Maj Leader 
Present- Bob Anthony, Min Leader 
Present - Tasha Hunt, Majority Whip 
Present - Tom Figlar, Minority Whip 
Present - Maurine Crouch 
Absent - Doug Foley 
 Present - Jeron Alston 
Present - Abdul Osmanu 
Present - Rhonda Caldwell 
Present - Grace Teodosio 
Present - Adrian Webber 
Present - Ted Stevens 
Present - Tameeka Parks  
 
1. CALL OF THE MEETING AND TAKING OF THE ROLL 
Legislative Council Regular Meeting, October 5, 2026.  President Kiely called the meeting 
to order at 7:40pm with the members noted above in attendance.  Council member Foley 
was absent.  
  Leadership Update –  
President Kiely reported that Leadership met to review the Budget Ordinance and 
discuss adjustments to the budget timeline. Majority Leader Gallagher announced that 
the Audit Committee would hold its organizational meeting on October 8. President 
Kiely also advised that Leadership is scheduling a meeting to develop a process for 
quarterly departmental reporting.  
      
 
 
Mayor's Report – 
Chief of Staff Peterson advised that the mayor had submitted comments to DEEP 
regarding the proposed Amazon drone program and reported that Amazon has 
postponed implementation pending additional meetings with community stakeholders. 
She also provided updates on recent and upcoming community events, clarified the 
hiring process for an item before the Council, and advised that two Submission 
Calendar items had been withdrawn for further review.  
      
 
 
News and Announcements –  
President Kiely announced several upcoming community events, including the 
Shepherd Glen Fall Festival on October 24, the Hamden Human Rights and Relations 
Commission's Teen Violence Prevention Discussion on October 20 and Journeys to 
America program on November 17, and the Newhall Foundation Repair and Former 
Middle School Demolition Community Meeting on October 29. She also recognized Six 
Lakes for its recent community trash cleanup efforts and thanked the organization for its 
continued commitment to the community.    
 
Councilwoman Hunt reminded residents of the upcoming Hamden Back to School 
Carnival and encouraged the community to attend in support of Hamden schools. 
       
2. REPORTS OF DEPARTMENTS, BOARDS, COMMISSIONS, AND COUNCIL LIAISONS  
 1. Report of Boards & Commission –
President Kiely reported that the Finance Commission met on October 1, 2026, and 
reviewed ongoing financial matters, including support for the audit process, an 
informational item, and the creation of a commission working group. 
      
 2. Update from Department Heads 
 
President Kiely highlighted the ARPA and Restricted Accounts Budget vs. Actual 
Reports and encouraged council members look them over. She mentioned the Board 
of Education’s funding request and noted that it would be heard in the Finance 
Committee this evening.  She also pointed out the BOE’s recent agendas and 
encouraged attendance.  
      
 3.  Council Liaison Reports 
 
REPORT OF UPDATED STANDING RULES PROPOSAL BY COUNSEL TO 
COUNCIL 
Attorney Mednick provided an overview of the proposed revisions to the Standing 
Rules.  
   
BOARD OF EDUCATION REVIEW OF FUNDING REQUEST 
Board of Education Chair Peter Downhour presented a request for $70,000 to fund a 
comprehensive special education needs assessment by WestEd. 
      
3. PUBLIC INPUT AND CORRESPONDENCE 
Six members of the public came forward to give public comment.  President Kiely also 
noted that we had received one item of written public comment.  The Public Input session 
was closed at 9:52pm.
